rows.question: How do I change the address on my driving licence?

answer.answer:
You can change the address on a full or provisional GB driving licence for free with DVLA, online or by post. You can keep driving while you wait for the new licence.

Online: Sign in to the GOV.UK "change address" service (you may need to prove your identity with photo ID such as a passport or driving licence). Your licence should arrive within a week.

By post (usually within 3 weeks; longer if DVLA needs to check identity or medical details):
- Photocard licence: complete the "changes" section on letter D741 that came with your licence, then send the licence and letter to DVLA, Swansea, SA99 1BN, with the correct postage. If you don't have the D741, use form D1 (cars/motorcycles) or D2 (lorries/buses), available from most Post Offices.
- Paper licence: send a completed D1 or D2, your driving licence, original documents confirming your identity, and a passport photograph, with the correct postage.

Also: change the address on your vehicle log book (V5C), update your vehicle tax Direct Debit if you pay that way, and update your personalised registration number document (V750 or V778) if you have one. You can be fined up to £1,000 if you don't tell DVLA about an address change.

If you're moving abroad, you can't register the new address on a British licence; contact the driving licence authority in your new country. Northern Ireland has a different process.

rows.question: How long do penalty points stay on my licence?

answer.answer:
Penalty points (endorsements) stay on your driving record for either 4 or 11 years, depending on the offence:
- Most offences: 4 years from the date of the offence (e.g. offence on 10 June 2012 stays until 10 June 2016).
- 4 years from the date of conviction for reckless/dangerous driving (codes DD40, DD60, DD80) and for offences that result in disqualification (e.g. conviction on 28 May 2011 stays until 28 May 2015).
- 11 years from the date of conviction for drink or drug driving (DR10, DR20, DR30, DR31, DR61, DR80) and causing death by careless driving under the influence or without providing a specimen (CD40, CD50, CD60, CD70) (e.g. conviction on 3 December 2009 stays until 3 December 2020).
Totting-up code TT99 stays for 4 years from conviction. The points are "valid" for the first 3 years (4-year endorsement) or 10 years (11-year endorsement); a court can consider them for a new offence during that time, and insurers and employers may see them for the periods the page describes. Check your exact removal date on your driving licence record.

rows.question: Which car insurance company is cheapest for a new driver?

answer.answer: The GOV.UK pages I searched do not name or compare insurance companies or say which is cheapest for new drivers. They only cover the legal requirement (third party insurance is the minimum), that you need your own policy when learning in your own car, and that some insurers require supervisors to be over 25. To compare prices, you would need to use an insurance comparison site or broker, which GOV.UK mentions only generally.

rows.question: How many times can I change my car driving test booking now?

answer.answer: You can change a car driving test booking 2 times (the limit applies since 31 March 2026; if you used changes under the old rules, you get 2 more from that date). Changing the date/time, test centre, or swapping counts as one change, even if you change several things together. Updating contact details or your instructor's reference number doesn't count, and DVSA-initiated changes reset your count to 2. After 2 changes you must cancel and rebook; a full refund is available if you cancel at least 10 full working days before the test. Other test types still allow 6 changes.
